query: LTX-2.3 audio path intermittently produces 'Input contains (near) NaN/+-Inf' from ffmpeg's AAC encoder: the AudioVAE generates NaNs at 'inconvenient' sequence lengths (e.g. 69/121 frames) that the vocoder amplifies, and fp16 attention backends worsen it.

desired.outcome: OP (ai-bond, flash-attention maintainer) traced it to ffmpeg receiving NaN/Inf and proposes sanitizing in comfy_api video_types.py (`torch.nan_to_num` + clamp before av.AudioFrame); diagnosis cross-referenced with #386/#475/#11664 but patch not merged or OP-run-confirmed.
desired.quality: Diagnosis identifies correct root cause; fix actionable and directionally correct.
desired.answer_guidance: OP (ai-bond, flash-attention maintainer) traced it to ffmpeg receiving NaN/Inf and proposes sanitizing in comfy_api video_types.py (`torch.nan_to_num` + clamp before av.AudioFrame); diagnosis cross-referenced with #386/#475/#11664 but patch not merged or OP-run-confirmed.
desired.guidance_note: Known fix from the original issue thread. Use to verify the diagnosis targets the right root cause; alternative fixes that resolve the same root cause are acceptable.

_tags.hidden_requirement: Trace intermittent AAC-encoder NaN/Inf failures to AudioVAE NaNs at awkward sequence lengths amplified by the vocoder, then design a sanitize-at-the-boundary patch (nan_to_num before av.AudioFrame).
